objects.description: No custom data types are defined in this header. It only includes other headers (./fuzztest/domain.h and ./fuzztest/fuzztest_macros.h) and contains include guards. Types that may be defined in the included headers are out of scope for this task.
No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. It only includes other headers and contains include guards.
No custom structs, classes, enums, or typedefs are defined in this header. The file declares free functions in the fuzztest namespace only.

A thread-compatible, non-thread-safe URBG implementation that integrates with Abseil's mocking mechanisms to draw distribution values from a provided fuzz data stream. It behaves like a BitGen for absl distributions while also providing a minimal PCG64-like engine for non-mockable calls. The first 8 bytes of the input may seed the internal engine. Move-only; copy is disabled. Construction requires an absl::Span<const uint8_t> that outlives the generator.

functions.name: ReadFilesFromDirectory
functions.description: Recursively reads all files under the directory specified by dir and returns their contents as a vector of single-element tuples of std::string, suitable for use with .WithSeeds(). Intended for seeding fuzz tests that take a single std::string parameter.
requirements: dir must reference a directory path.
The returned vector elements are 1-tuples of std::string (content of each file), matching .WithSeeds() expectations for a single-argument (std::string) property function.
Exact traversal behavior and error handling for unreadable files or directories are not documented in this header (unknown).

functions.name: ReadFilesFromDirectory
functions.description: Recursively reads files under dir whose file names satisfy filter(name) and returns their contents as a vector of single-element tuples of std::string, suitable for use with .WithSeeds(). Enables selecting files by name pattern (e.g., only .xml files).
requirements: dir must reference a directory path.
filter must be a callable taking std::string_view (file name) and returning bool; only files for which filter(name) is true are included.
The returned vector elements are 1-tuples of std::string (content of each file), matching .WithSeeds() expectations for a single-argument (std::string) property function.
Exact traversal behavior and error handling for unreadable files or directories are not documented in this header (unknown).

functions.name: ParseDictionary
functions.description: Parses fuzzer dictionary definitions from text in the LibFuzzer dictionary format and returns the parsed entries. Returns an error status if the dictionary is in the wrong format.
requirements: text must be in the format specified at https://llvm.org/docs/LibFuzzer.html#dictionaries.
Callers must handle the error case via the returned absl::StatusOr (check status before use).
Specific limits (e.g., entry size/count) are not documented in this header (unknown).

functions.name: ReadDictionaryFromFile
functions.description: Reads dictionary entries from dictionary_file and returns them as a vector suitable for .WithDictionary(). The file is expected to be in the LibFuzzer dictionary format.
requirements: dictionary_file should point to a file in the format specified at https://llvm.org/docs/LibFuzzer.html#dictionaries.
Error handling behavior for missing/invalid files is not documented in this header (unknown).

functions.name: ToByteArray
functions.description: Converts the bytes of str into a std::vector<uint8_t>. Useful when interacting with LLVM fuzzer interfaces that require raw byte arrays.
requirements: str is treated as a sequence of bytes; encoding/character set is not interpreted.
No additional preconditions are documented.

functions.name: SkipTestsOrCurrentInput
functions.description: Skips execution depending on context: when called during fixture setup (constructor or SetUp()), it skips calling property functions until teardown; when called inside a property function, it skips adding the current input to the corpus during fuzzing. Intended to be used sparingly for efficiency and engine limitations.
requirements: May be called during fixture setup (constructor or SetUp()) to skip property function calls until teardown (destructor or TearDown()).
May be called inside a property function to skip adding the current input to the corpus.
Should not be called frequently due to engine limitations and efficiency reasons.

functions.name: fuzztest::internal_no_adl::InRegexp
functions.description: Constructs and returns a fuzztest domain of strings constrained to match the given regular expression. The regex syntax is that accepted by RE2. Typical usage is to generate or constrain string inputs that must match a specific pattern (e.g., dates, identifiers). Return type is an internal domain type (deduced via auto).
requirements: The regex argument must use syntax accepted by RE2.
The function is intended to produce a domain of strings whose values are sentences of the provided regular expression.

functions.name: fuzztest::internal_no_adl::ProtobufOf
functions.signature: template <typename PrototypeMessageProvider, typename T = std::remove_cv_t<std::remove_pointer_t<decltype(std::declval<PrototypeMessageProvider>()())>>> auto fuzztest::internal_no_adl::ProtobufOf(PrototypeMessageProvider get_prototype)
functions.description: Creates and returns a fuzztest domain that generates std::unique_ptr<Message> instances for the protobuf prototype (default instance) provided by the zero-argument callable get_prototype. Works for both concrete protobuf message classes and pointers to google::protobuf::Message. Use this to fuzz protobuf inputs derived from a specific message type.
requirements: get_prototype must be callable with no arguments.
get_prototype must return a pointer to a protobuf Message (or a derived message type).
REQUIRES: get_prototype never returns nullptr.
get_prototype is expected to return a prototype (default instance) for the desired message type.

functions.name: fuzztest::internal::GoogleTestFixtureAdapter::SetUp
functions.description: Overrides testing::Test::SetUp() in the GoogleTestFixtureAdapter partial specialization. It simply forwards to the base fixture’s SetUp() by calling Fixture::SetUp(). Intended to let the adapted GoogleTest fixture participate correctly in the GoogleTest lifecycle when used with fuzztest’s fixture adapters.
requirements: This member exists only for GoogleTestFixtureAdapter<Fixture, InstantiationType, ...> where Fixture is derived from ::testing::Test and InstantiationType is derived from ::fuzztest::internal::FixtureWithExplicitSetUp.
Must be called by the GoogleTest framework as part of the test lifecycle; it is not intended to be invoked directly by user test code.
The underlying Fixture::SetUp() must be valid to call and should leave the fixture in a ready state for the test body.

functions.name: fuzztest::internal::GoogleTestFixtureAdapter::TearDown
functions.description: Overrides testing::Test::TearDown() in the GoogleTestFixtureAdapter partial specialization. It forwards to the base fixture’s TearDown() by calling Fixture::TearDown(). Ensures the adapted fixture tears down correctly under the GoogleTest lifecycle.
requirements: This member exists only for GoogleTestFixtureAdapter<Fixture, InstantiationType, ...> where Fixture is derived from ::testing::Test and InstantiationType is derived from ::fuzztest::internal::FixtureWithExplicitSetUp.
Must be called by the GoogleTest framework as part of the test lifecycle; it is not intended to be invoked directly by user test code.
The underlying Fixture::TearDown() must be valid to call and should release or reset any resources acquired during SetUp() or the test.

functions.name: fuzztest::internal::GoogleTestFixtureAdapter::SetUpTestSuite
functions.description: Static suite-level setup for the adapted fixture. This forwards to Fixture::SetUpTestSuite() so any suite-scoped initialization on the original GoogleTest fixture is honored when used with fuzztest’s adapters.
requirements: This member exists only for GoogleTestFixtureAdapter<Fixture, InstantiationType, ...> where Fixture is derived from ::testing::Test and InstantiationType is derived from ::fuzztest::internal::FixtureWithExplicitSetUp.
Expected to be called by the GoogleTest framework before any tests in the suite run; not intended for manual invocation.
Fixture::SetUpTestSuite() (or the default provided by testing::Test) must be safe to call once per test suite and should prepare any suite-scoped resources.

functions.name: fuzztest::internal::GoogleTestFixtureAdapter::TearDownTestSuite
functions.description: Static suite-level teardown for the adapted fixture. This forwards to Fixture::TearDownTestSuite() to properly release any suite-scoped resources when using fuzztest’s adapters.
requirements: This member exists only for GoogleTestFixtureAdapter<Fixture, InstantiationType, ...> where Fixture is derived from ::testing::Test and InstantiationType is derived from ::fuzztest::internal::FixtureWithExplicitSetUp.
Expected to be called by the GoogleTest framework after all tests in the suite run; not intended for manual invocation.
Fixture::TearDownTestSuite() (or the default provided by testing::Test) must be safe to call once per test suite and should release any suite-scoped resources.

functions.name: fuzztest::ParseAbslFlags
functions.description: Initializes all Abseil (Abseil/absl) flags so FuzzTest can rely on them. It reads the provided command-line arguments but does not modify argv. Use this when you do not have other code (e.g., absl::ParseCommandLine()) initializing Abseil flags. Safe to call even if non-Abseil flags are present on the command line.
requirements: Call this only if no other code initializes Abseil flags from the command line (e.g., do not also call absl::ParseCommandLine()).
Pass the argc and argv as provided by main (argv is read-only for this function).
The function may be called after program start; there is no requirement that main has already registered tests, but caller should ensure flags are not already initialized by other means.

functions.name: fuzztest::InitFuzzTest
functions.signature: void fuzztest::InitFuzzTest(int* argc, char*** argv, std::string_view binary_id = {})
functions.description: Initializes FuzzTest: processes FuzzTest-related flags and registers FUZZ_TESTs in the binary as GoogleTest TESTs. The argc/argv pointers are accepted to support compatibility mode with external engines via LLVMFuzzerRunDriver. The optional binary_id overrides the default binary identifier used to locate the saved corpus for this binary (defaults to the binary filename).
requirements: REQUIRES: main() has started before calling this function.
REQUIRES: Abseil flags must have been initialized beforehand (via fuzztest::ParseAbslFlags or other means).
Provide valid pointers to argc (non-null) and argv (non-null pointer to a char** as received from main).
If overriding, binary_id should identify this binary consistently to locate its corpus.

functions.name: fuzztest::ListRegisteredTests
functions.description: Returns the list of all registered fuzz test full names in the form "<suite_name>.<property_function_name>". Intended for discovery or selection UIs/tools after FuzzTest initialization.
requirements: REQUIRES: main() has started before calling this function.

functions.name: fuzztest::GetMatchingFuzzTestOrExit
functions.description: Resolves a provided name specification to a single registered fuzz test’s full name. The specification can be: an exact full name (e.g., "Suite.Test"), a strict substring that matches exactly one test, or an empty string (which selects the only test if exactly one exists). If no single match is found, the function exits the process with an error message.
requirements: REQUIRES: main() has started before calling this function.
Caller must be prepared for the process to exit if the specification does not resolve to exactly one test.
Accepts an empty name only if there is exactly one fuzz test in the binary.

functions.name: fuzztest::RunSpecifiedFuzzTest
functions.description: Runs the specified FUZZ_TEST in fuzzing mode until a bug is found or execution is manually stopped. The test to run is selected using GetMatchingFuzzTestOrExit(name). The binary_id identifies the corpus location for the fuzz test(s) in this binary.
requirements: REQUIRES: main() has started before calling this function.
REQUIRES: The binary must be built with SanCov (Sanitizer Coverage) instrumentation enabled.
If name does not resolve to exactly one FUZZ_TEST, the function will exit; callers should not expect a return in that case.
Provide a valid binary_id identifying the binary’s corpus namespace.

functions.name: fuzztest::FuzzingBitGen::FuzzingBitGen
functions.description: Constructs a FuzzingBitGen that reads an unowned fuzzed data byte stream used to drive distribution outputs and to seed an internal URBG for non-mockable calls. The data stream is treated as a sequence of distribution-specific variates. The first 8 bytes are used to seed an internal PRNG for calls not captured through mockable Abseil distribution methods. Use when you want deterministic, data-driven random behavior for fuzzing infrastructure.
requirements: The provided absl::Span<const uint8_t> data_stream must outlive the FuzzingBitGen instance (unowned).
This type is thread-compatible but not thread-safe; callers must provide external synchronization if accessed from multiple threads.
The first 8 bytes of the data stream are used to seed an internal URBG for non-mockable calls; behavior if fewer than 8 bytes are provided is unknown (not specified in this header).
When the data stream is exhausted, Abseil MockingBitGen-backed calls will continue to return an arbitrary legal value (typically minimum or mean of the distribution).

functions.name: fuzztest::FuzzingBitGen::min
functions.description: Returns the minimum value producible by this URBG’s result_type (uint64_t). Useful for templated code expecting a URBG interface.
requirements: No preconditions; callable without an instance (static).

functions.name: fuzztest::FuzzingBitGen::max
functions.description: Returns the maximum value producible by this URBG’s result_type (uint64_t). Useful for templated code expecting a URBG interface.
requirements: No preconditions; callable without an instance (static).

functions.name: fuzztest::FuzzingBitGen::seed
functions.description: Seeds the internal URBG state with the provided 64-bit value. Intended to reinitialize the underlying engine (PCG-like) used for generating values via operator() and non-mockable paths.
requirements: May be called on an initialized instance to reset its internal URBG state.
This type is thread-compatible but not thread-safe; callers must synchronize concurrent calls to seed or other methods on the same instance.
seed_value is a 64-bit unsigned integer; no further constraints are specified.

functions.name: fuzztest::FuzzingBitGen::operator()
functions.description: Generates and returns the next 64-bit pseudorandom value from the internal URBG (a minimal PCG64-like engine). This satisfies the UniformRandomBitGenerator interface expected by standard algorithms.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, constructed FuzzingBitGen instance.
This type is thread-compatible but not thread-safe; concurrent calls on the same instance must be externally synchronized.

data_types.description: A raw sequence of bytes with no required encoding or structure. May contain any 8-bit values from 0x00 to 0xFF, including embedded NULs and non-UTF-8 sequences. Used wherever input is treated purely as bytes rather than text.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target format: arbitrary byte string (no structure). Used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# Goal: Provide interesting yet valid byte sequences that exercise ToByteArray,
# including edge cases (empty, small sizes), varying lengths, and full 0x00-0xFF range.
# Keep size <= 4096 bytes.

_MAX_SIZE = 4096

# Predefined interesting seeds: cover ASCII, UTF-8, binary, patterns, lengths.
_INTERESTING_PAYLOADS: List[bytes] = [
    b"",  # empty
    b"a",  # single byte
    b"\x00",  # NUL
    b"\xff",  # max byte
    b"\x00\x00\x00\x00",  # zeros
    b"\xff\xff\xff\xff",  # ones (0xFF)
    b"\x00\xff\x00\xff\x00\xff\x00\xff",  # alternating
    b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog",  # ASCII sentence
    "Привет, мир!".encode("utf-8"),  # UTF-8 multibyte
    b"\x00hello\x00world\x00",  # embedded NULs
    bytes(range(256)),  # 0..255 once
    bytes(range(255, -1, -1)),  # 255..0 once
    b"A" * 1,  # length 1 boundary
    b"B" * 16,  # typical small block size
    b"C" * 255,  # 255 boundary
    b"D" * 256,  # 256 boundary
    b"E" * 1024,  # 1 KiB
    b"F" * 2048,  # 2 KiB
]

# Simple pattern generators to expand variety deterministically from seed

def _gen_repeated_block(rng: random.Random, block: bytes, total_len: int) -> bytes:
    if total_len <= 0:
        return b""
    reps = (total_len + len(block) - 1) // len(block)
    data = (block * reps)[:total_len]
    return data


def _gen_gradient(rng: random.Random, length: int, start: int = None, step: int = None) -> bytes:
    if length <= 0:
        return b""
    if start is None:
        start = rng.randrange(256)
    if step is None:
        # Odd step to maximize coverage before cycling
        step = rng.randrange(1, 256, 2)
    arr = bytearray(length)
    val = start
    for i in range(length):
        arr[i] = val & 0xFF
        val = (val + step) & 0xFF
    return bytes(arr)


def _gen_markov_like(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    # Produce runs with occasional flips to new random byte
    if length <= 0:
        return b""
    data = bytearray(length)
    cur = rng.randrange(256)
    i = 0
    while i < length:
        run = 1 + int(rng.expovariate(1/8))  # avg run ~8
        run = min(run, length - i)
        for _ in range(run):
            data[i] = cur
            i += 1
            if i >= length:
                break
        if i < length:
            # Small mutation in value
            if rng.random() < 0.6:
                cur = (cur + rng.choice([-1, 1, -2, 2, -16, 16])) & 0xFF
            else:
                cur = rng.randrange(256)
    return bytes(data)


def _gen_structured_prefix(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create a header-like prefix that resembles sizes/lengths, then payload.
    # While ToByteArray does not parse, some consumers may feed such strings elsewhere.
    # Layout: [magic 4][len16 2][len32 4][flags 2][seed 8][payload]
    magic_choices = [b"\x7fELF", b"PK\x03\x04", b"%PDF", b"\x89PNG", b"\x00\x00\x00\x00"]
    magic = rng.choice(magic_choices)
    remaining = _MAX_SIZE - len(magic) - (2 + 4 + 2 + 8)
    payload_len = rng.randrange(0, max(1, remaining))
    flags = rng.randrange(0, 65536)
    seed = rng.getrandbits(64)
    len16 = min(payload_len, 0xFFFF)
    len32 = payload_len & 0xFFFFFFFF
    payload = _gen_markov_like(rng, payload_len)
    return b"".join([
        magic,
        struct.pack("<H", len16),
        struct.pack("<I", len32),
        struct.pack("<H", flags),
        struct.pack("<Q", seed),
        payload,
    ])


def _choose_length(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Biased distribution favoring interesting boundaries
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 511, 512, 1023, 1024, 2047, 2048]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(choices)
    return rng.randint(0, _MAX_SIZE)


def _compose_bytes(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # With some probability, pick a predefined payload
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        base = rng.choice(_INTERESTING_PAYLOADS)
        # Optionally trim or extend via repetition to hit sizes
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            target = _choose_length(rng)
            if target <= len(base):
                return base[:target]
            else:
                return _gen_repeated_block(rng, base if base else b"\x00", target)
        return base

    # Generate from patterns
    mode = rng.choice(["gradient", "runs", "repeat", "structured"])  # diversify
    if mode == "gradient":
        length = _choose_length(rng)
        return _gen_gradient(rng, length)
    if mode == "runs":
        length = _choose_length(rng)
        return _gen_markov_like(rng, length)
    if mode == "repeat":
        length = _choose_length(rng)
        block_len = rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16, 32])
        block = bytes(rng.randrange(256) for _ in range(block_len))
        return _gen_repeated_block(rng, block, length)
    # structured
    return _gen_structured_prefix(rng)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    data = _compose_bytes(rng)
    # Ensure cap
    if len(data) > _MAX_SIZE:
        data = data[:_MAX_SIZE]
    return data
